Implementation Plan

Implementation Plan for #6781: hold back automatic `/approved` on plans that list automation paths, behind `AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED`

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends check_automation_paths
Scope-mode justification: The unblock judge's operator step for #6769 sets the scope, and this plan sticks to it. Three places post an automatic `/approved` on a fresh plan: the "Auto-approve clear plan" step in `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, and the `auto_approve` arms of the managed and standalone stall-recovery loops in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. Each one gets a gate keyed on the automation paths the plan lists. The gate is off by default. While it is off, a plan that lists automation paths is not auto-approved; ordinary plans behave as before. When it is on, the gate uses the existing classifier (`is_automation_path`), the trusted exact-grant builder (`build_automation_grant`) and the denial function (`check_automation_paths`) in `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py`. It denies and reports every protected path that is not granted, and auto-approves only when every listed path is granted. The implementation-time guard (`IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD` in `implement.yml` and `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh`) is not changed. The complete version (both poller arms, report output, tests for both outcomes) costs under 30 LOC more than a plan.yml-only shortcut. Neither adds a dependency or an external interface, so per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed) the complete version is chosen. The flag is not enabled anywhere.

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = 08c4132ec756bf6acc2c12a1602a19d441de0ff2, branch `main`. There is no integration-branch metadata, so the target is `main` and there is no mismatch.

Conflicts with the issue:
- The issue says "backport that guard if targeting stable". This issue targets `main` (no `Integration branch:` / `Target branch: stable` line), so the backport does not apply. The issue also notes that the stable-branch guard lacks `build_automation_grant` / `check_automation_paths`. Shipping to `stable` therefore goes through the normal promote cycle, which carries the guard functions and this gate together. Nothing is cherry-picked.
- The issue body has no `files_touched:` block. Every file this plan changes under `scripts/` and `.github/` is an automation path, so the unchanged implement-time guard will reject the commit (`reason=no_allowlist`) until a trusted author adds an exact grant. See the self-check below.

Files likely to change:
- `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py`: new plan-approval mode, reusing the existing grant and check functions.
- `.github/workflows/plan.yml`: the "Auto-approve clear plan" step, its env, and the support-script staging list.
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`: a new shared gate helper, called from the managed and standalone `auto_approve` arms.
- `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`: add `files_touched_scope_guard.py` to the staged-script list (`targeted_file_context.py` is already there), and add the flag env to the poller step(s) that run stall recovery.
- `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`: unit tests for the new mode.
- `tests/test_plan_auto_approve_safe_state_fetch.py`: contract and behaviour tests for the plan.yml gate.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`: sandboxed poller cases for both arms.
- `README.md`: one row in the Variables table.
- `agents.md`: one paragraph in "Implement scope-lock label".
- `changelog.d/6781-automation-path-plan-auto-approval.md`: new changelog fragment.

Functions or modules to implement:

1. `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py`
   - `extract_plan_automation_paths(plan_text) -> list[str]`
     - Import `extract_paths_from_plan` and `LIKELY_HEADER_RE` from `targeted_file_context` lazily, inside the function only. The implement run's staged copy of this script does not depend on `targeted_file_context`, so a module-level import could break it.
     - Keep the paths where `is_automation_path` is true, normalized with `normalize_path`.
     - Fail closed in two cases:
       - If the plan has no "Files likely to change"-style header, scan every backticked token in the whole plan for automation-path prefixes.
       - Inside the section, a token whose first segment is protected but that the path normalizer rejects (a glob, a trailing `/`) is still kept as protected. The exact-grant check can never cover it, so it is always denied.
   - `evaluate_plan_auto_approval(plan_text, enabled, issue_meta, pipeline_login, allow_workflow_edits, issue_number) -> dict`
     - Returns `{"schema_version": "plan_auto_approval.v1", "decision": "allow"|"defer", "reason": ..., "protected_paths": [...], "ungranted_paths": [...]}`.
     - No protected paths: `allow`, reason `no_automation_paths`. Ordinary plans are unchanged.
     - Protected paths with the flag off: `defer`, reason `flag_disabled`. All protected paths are reported as ungranted, because no grant check runs.
     - Protected paths with the flag on: `grant = build_automation_grant(issue_meta, pipeline_login)`, then `check_automation_paths(protected, grant, allow_workflow_edits, str(issue_number))`.
       - `in-scope`: `allow`, reason `granted`.
       - Otherwise: `defer` with the returned reason and the full denied list (`path_not_granted`, `no_allowlist`, `untrusted_author`, `workflow_edits_disabled`, `grant_issue_mismatch`, ...).
   - New CLI mode: `--check-plan-auto-approval --plan-file P --approval-enabled true|false [--issue-meta-file F --pipeline-login L --allow-workflow-edits V --issue-number N] [--result-out J]`.
     - Prints the JSON result and writes it to `--result-out` when given.
     - Exits `0` on allow and `EXIT_AUTOMATION_UNGRANTED` (30) on defer.
     - An unreadable plan, bad metadata JSON or a missing import gives `defer` with reason `evaluation_error` and exit 30. It never fails open.
   - The flag value is normalized the same way as the other boolean flags: `1|true|yes|on`, case-insensitive. Anything else counts as off.

2. `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, step "Auto-approve clear plan" (`id: auto_approve`)
   - Add env:
     - `AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED: ${{ vars.AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED || 'false' }}`
     - `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS: ${{ vars.ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS || 'true' }}`
   - Position: after the existing open / trusted-author checks and inside the `1|true|yes|on` arm, before the `sleep 3` / POST.
   - Write `CURRENT_ISSUE_JSON` (already fetched live in this step, so no extra issue read) to a temp file and run the new CLI mode against `${CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE}`. That is the plan text before the "To proceed reply: /approved" footer.
   - Read the pipeline login with `gh api user --jq .login` only when the flag is on and protected paths exist. That is at most one extra call, and none on the default path.
   - On `defer`:
     - Log `AI_PHASE_GATE_V1 phase=plan gate=auto_approve reason=automation_paths_<reason> outcome=defer issue=N`.
     - Log `IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD mode=plan_auto_approve outcome=defer reason=<r> issue=N count=<k>`, which reuses an existing stable prefix.
     - Post one report comment starting with `<!-- ai:plan-auto-approval-deferred:v1 -->`. It lists every ungranted path (backticked, with backticks in path text escaped), the reason, and tells the operator to add exact `files_touched:` entries and reply `/approved`.
     - Leave `auto_approved=false`. The existing "Telegram plan notification" step then fires, since it is already gated on `auto_approved != 'true'`.
   - On `allow`: run the existing POST unchanged.
   - Add `files_touched_scope_guard.py` and `targeted_file_context.py` to the `for f in ...` staging list at line ~286. A missing script then fails the staging step, as for every other required support script.

3. `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
   - `_plan_auto_approval_gate <issue_num> <comments_json> <issue_meta_json_or_empty>`
     - Takes the newest trusted plan comment from the comments array. It uses the same selector `implement.yml` "Extract implementation plan" uses: body matches `(?im)^\s*implementation\s+plan\b`, and the author is `github-actions[bot]` / `codex-bot[bot]` as Bot, or OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR.
     - Writes that body to a `RUNTIME_DIR` temp file and runs `python3 "${ORCH_SCRIPTS_ROOT}/files_touched_scope_guard.py" --check-plan-auto-approval ...`.
     - When the flag is on and protected paths exist, it reads issue metadata once (`repos/.../issues/N`) and the pipeline login. The login is cached in a cycle-local variable (`_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_PIPELINE_LOGIN`), so it is read at most once per tick.
     - Returns 0 on allow and 1 on defer. A missing plan comment, a missing script or any error is a defer.
     - Logs `IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD mode=plan_auto_approve outcome=<allow|defer> reason=<r> issue=N count=<k>`.
   - Managed `auto_approve` arm (`execute_stall_recovery_action`, ~line 14709): call the gate after the staged-support latch check and before "Auto-approving plan...". It reuses the already-fetched `_managed_staged_support_comments` (cached or paginated via `_staged_support_comments_for_guard`), so the default path adds no API call. On defer, log `STALL_SKIP issue=N reason=automation_paths_require_approval phase=${phase} action=none` and `return 1`, the same pattern as the latch skip: no increment, no `/approved`, no Telegram.
   - Standalone `auto_approve` arm (~line 18112): call the gate with the loop's existing `comments_json`. On defer, log the same `STALL_SKIP` line and skip the POST, leaving `took_action` and `STALL_RECOVERY_SHOULD_INCREMENT` false. Use whichever `continue` / flag form fits the surrounding `case` without falling through to the alert.
   - Defaults inside the script: `AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED="${AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED:-false}
